title: Counting the Nights a Resort Lodging Party Gave Up
content:
How the nights a Resort Lodging party gave up are counted follows the records of the stay: the nights the reservation covers, the nights the folio shows consumed, and the departure recorded on the reservation.

Where a departure is recorded on the reservation and the folio shows fewer nights consumed than the nights from the arrival date to that departure, the nights given up are counted as the nights the reservation covers less the nights from the arrival date to the recorded departure, because the departure is the firm record of when the unit came back.

Where a departure is recorded on the reservation and the folio shows a night consumed for every night from the arrival date to that departure, the nights given up are counted as the nights the reservation covers less the nights the folio shows consumed.

Where neither holds, no night of the stay counts as given up.

| What the records show | The nights given up |
| --- | --- |
| A departure recorded, fewer nights consumed than from arrival to that departure | the nights the reservation covers, less the nights from arrival to the recorded departure |
| A departure recorded, a night consumed for every night from arrival to that departure | the nights the reservation covers, less the nights the folio shows consumed |
| Neither | none |

### Three hypothetical stays on a reservation covering 7 nights

A departure recorded 5 nights after the arrival date, with the folio showing 3 nights consumed, shows fewer nights consumed than those 5, so the nights given up are the 7 the reservation covers less those 5, which is 2.

A departure recorded 5 nights after the arrival date, with the folio showing 5 nights consumed, shows a night consumed for every night from arrival to the departure, so the nights given up are the 7 less the 5 consumed, which is again 2.

A reservation carrying no recorded departure at all answers neither of the two, and no night of the stay counts as given up.
